one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event inside the window: the Q3 FY27 print (quarter ended 2026-10-31), expected ~Wed 2026-12-02 after close and so priced in the 2026-12-03 close. The company has not announced the date yet; last year it announced on 2025-11-03 for 2025-12-03 [27], so a notice should come any day. Guide: product 1,588-1,593, non-GAAP op margin 15.5%, 382M shares [6]. The company beat its product guide 10 of 10 quarters (median +4.6%) and its margin guide 10 of 10 (median +3.0 pt). The approved set has 1,617.7 / 16.8%, a smaller beat than usual because the CFO says the guide only forecasts 'observed behavior' and calls ~3% 'a very solid beat' [25], and Observe now sits in the base. A beat is expected (Street EPS 0.60 vs whisper 0.71), so the price reaction turns on the FY27 Q4 implied guide and cRPO/RPO (bookings weighted to Q4 [26]). Risk: a ~286M loss on the 2027-note repurchase could land in Q3 GAAP and possibly non-GAAP other income. Earnings moves have been large (+23% after Q2). I use a lognormal with median 298 (+0.7% drift for the beat habit and post-surprise drift) and sigma 0.20, a little above annual vol / 3.5 = 0.183 because this is an earnings month. Nothing else is scheduled; the macro prints are the 2026-11-07 jobs report and CPI mid-November.

fair_value.method: Approved quarterly driver build gives ~9.8B NTM revenue at 2027-11-03; at 12.62x EV/NTM sales (k-rule on a 7.14x NTM-on-EV peer median) plus ~3.2B net cash at the horizon over 388.7M non-GAAP diluted shares = $324.1. The SBC-costed owner-earnings check ($111) carries weight 0.

Q3 FY27 128%, Q4 129%: the reported rate is trailing-12-month and lags the quarters (quarterly product growth 33.9%/36.8% in Q1/Q2 FY27 vs TTM product growth 31.1%/32.6% and NRR 126% [5,6]; the Q3 guide is +37-38% y/y [6]), so the TTM rate rises as H2 FY27 rolls in (CFO: third consecutive quarter of acceleration, existing-customer consumption is the driver [6,7]). FY28 revenue 8.29B (+30%), FY29 10.30B (+24%), non-GAAP margin 17.6% / 19.4%. EV/NTM sales de-rates from 14.55x to 12.62x (k-rule), net cash builds to ~3.2B.

The SBC-costed owner-earnings check now deducts SBC as cost on a non-growing 388.7M share count (round 1 also grew shares: double count, fixed) and carries weight 0. TTM FCF less SBC: 1,195 - 1,642 = -447.

reasoning: Round 2. Supervisor findings accepted: (a) exit EV/sales on the k = 0.8 rule over a cleaned NTM-consensus-on-EV peer median (7.14x; MDB/DDOG consensus re-opened on StockAnalysis), so 12.62x instead of my 11.0x: my extra growth haircut had no tested evidence and the deceleration is already in the NTM revenue it multiplies; (b) the owner-earnings leg double-counted SBC (cost plus 418.9M shares): now 111.2 on 388.7M, weight 0 per the software blend-weight test; (c) cash roll now has depreciation 2.5% (not 4.7%, which includes acquired-intangible amortization already outside non-GAAP EBIT), capex 1.5%, deferred-revenue NWC -0.30 and buybacks 600/650: net cash at H ~3.2B vs 2.5B. Where I differ: no non-GAAP P/E leg (gap_note). Scenarios: approved driver deltas (nrr -4/+3 pt, new_cust -25%/+20%, product_gm -2/+1 pt) plus multiple -5.5x/+4.0x: P10 169 / P90 454, a fatter left tail (log spreads 0.51 / 0.26 per z) consistent with 64% realized vol and SNOW's own history.  I read the Q2 FY27 release and 10-Q, the 2026-10-01 convertible 8-K, the FY25/FY26 Q4 releases (first annual guides), the Q1 FY27 corrected call transcript, the June 2026 Investor Day deck and a summary of the Q2 call. Fetches were limited to 6 under the shared budget, and Twelve Data statistics and estimates are not on this plan. Guidance record: the quarterly product guide was beaten 10/10 (median +4.6%) and the annual first guide by +6.5% (FY25) and +4.5% (FY26). But the FY27 guide has already been raised twice (5,660 -> 6,070), and the CFO says the guide only forecasts 'observed behavior' and that ~3% is 'a very solid beat'. So I accept the approved set's smaller H2 beat (FY27 product 6,136, +1.1% over the guide, ~0.5% over the Street) and do not argue against any driver. My view against the drivers by id: nrr's rise to 128-129% is plausible (TTM lag); the risk is in the FY29-30 fade, which I would not take lower. new_cust's drop from 118 to ~70 a quarter is conservative given 692 net adds and Observe. product_gm 73.5-74.5% is fair after the 75 -> 74% guide cut. opex_pct's leverage is backed by 17 organic hires in Q1. ps_rev doesn't matter.

drivers.derivation: FY27 guide 74.0% on product guide 6,070 [6] implies H2 GP 4,491.8 - H1 2,116.8 = 2,375 on H2 product 3,243.8 = 73.2%; the company beat its FY26 guide (75% -> 75.8%), so Q3 74.0%, Q4 73.5% (FY27 74.3%). quarters.note: Forecast quarters: product revenue = lines.prod = ly_prod x nrr + new_cust (NRR identity; ly_prod reads the line's own history, so scenario moves compound); revenue = product + ps_rev; ebit (company non-GAAP operating income) = product revenue x product_gm + ps_rev x ps_gm - revenue x opex_pct; sbc = sbc_pct x rev (constant path). constants.prod_actual = reported product revenue for the actual quarters Q1 FY26-Q2 FY27 (Ex.99.1 [1-6]); later values unused. constants.ps_gm = non-GAAP professional services gross margin -8% (H1 FY27 (8.882) / 111.554 = -8.0% [6]; FY26 +0.049 / 211.6 = 0.0% [4]). other_income and ng_diluted_shares are for the EPS check in notes_nrr.md only. constants.prod_ly (product revenue a year earlier, base path) is kept only as the weight for product_gm's year average (wmean); values use lines.prod.
